text:
anya: Quick thread  discussing inline rollback actions in the version history timeline. Two competing ideas: inline confirm (compact, stays in-context) vs modal confirm (safer, more explanatory). Need input on microcopy, keyboard flow, and undo toast behaviour.

rachel: In last week's usability, people liked not losing context. Inline confirm keeps timeline visible which helps pick the right point to revert to.

tom: Risk: accidental clicks. Inline confirm is more prone to mis-taps on touch. We need a guard that is lightweight but robust.

matt: Engineering note: inline confirm is easier to implement layout-wise, but modal gives us space for extra metadata (who, snapshot diff) which helps users be confident.

peter: Proposal 1: Inline confirm button replaces the rollback button with a compact two-state control: "Rollback" -> "Confirm rollback". Hitting confirm triggers server call and shows an undo toast for 30s.

peter: Proposal 2: Small modal with a short summary + 2-step confirm. After action, show undo toast as well. Modal required for orgs with stricter policies.

anya: Copy question: do we say "Rollback to this version" vs "Revert to this snapshot"? Which is clearer for non-experts?

rachel: I prefer "Revert to this version". "Rollback" can sound scary. Also shorter copy fits the tight UI better.

tom: For accessibility, ensure the inline confirm is reachable by keyboard tabbing and that focus moves into the confirm control. Also add aria-describedby linking to the snippet explaining what will change.

matt: Undo toast design: subtle, bottom-right on desktop, bottom on mobile. It must include the change summary and an accessible "Undo" control. Audit: can we support a keyboard shortcut to dismiss the toast and trigger undo?

aria-bot: Accessibility checklist: 1) when inline confirm appears, use role="alertdialog" or set focus to it, 2) ensure cancel is reachable, 3) announce the transition with aria-live="assertive", 4) toast must be focusable and in tab order, 5) provide clear labels like "Revert to v1.3 — undo".

anay: [typo] — correction: anya: Also consider focus return: after undo or confirm, focus should go back to the timeline item to avoid context loss.

peter: Telemetry plan: record which flow used (inline vs modal), confirm time, accidental cancels, and undo rate. Run an A/B test for 2 weeks. Key metrics: time-to-rollback, rate of undo, and support tickets opened within 24h.

rachel: UI nuance: for dense timelines the inline confirm may cause layout shift. Maybe use an overlay card anchored to the item (keeps context but avoids pushing content).

tom: For touch devices, add a small delay to guard confirm activation or require a two-tap pattern: first tap opens compact summary, second tap confirms. That balances speed and safety.

matt: For modal approach, we can prefetch diff data to keep the confirm fast. For inline, show a mini diff snippet (truncated) with a "show more" link.

anya: Action items:
- Design: mock three variants (inline two-state, anchored card, modal) with copy options: "Revert to this version", "Restore snapshot", "Rollback to here".
- Research: quick microtest with 6 internal reviewers on desktop + 6 on mobile.
- Eng: instrument telemetry flags for A/B and add undo endpoint for 30s grace.
- A11y: SR walkthrough and keyboard focus flow tests.

matt: I'll scope the telemetry event keys and add to the rollout plan.

rachel: I'll prototype the anchored card in figma and post links. Want copy suggestions: short + low-alarm.

peter: Also suggest an org-level policy toggle to force modal confirmation for enterprise tenants.

anya: Great — I'll schedule this for design review on Friday and add the three mocks to the agenda. Thanks all :rocket:

aria-bot: Accessibility review requested; tentative window booked for 3 days from now.

matt: cool.

rachel: thanks team.
